newsitem.title: UK: RTZ-CRA says Sumitomo copper crisis hit shares.
newsitem.headline: RTZ-CRA says Sumitomo copper crisis hit shares.

text.p: Shares in mining giant RTZ-CRA were hit in the short term by the Sumitomo Corp copper scandal which broke in mid-June, according to RTZ-CRA chief executive Robert Wilson.
"I think it's probably done a bit of damage in the short term," he told reporters at a news briefing on Thursday.
But the longer term effect was not great, he added.
World prices of copper, one of RTZ-CRA's most important products, fell sharply before and after the June 13 announcement that it had run up $1.8 billion losses in unauthorised copper trade.
On Thursday RTZ-CRA announced a 22 percent drop in first-half 1996 net adjusted earnings to $552 million. The largest single factor was a fall in quoted metal prices.
Wilson said he could not rule out similar occurences to the Sumitomo losses in future on the metal markets.
One problem was the proliferation of over-the-counter derivates which were hard to monitor and control, he said.
"That is going to be something difficult to control," Wilson said. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 8057
